rules.sentence: Radial neuropathy: Perioperative radial neuropathy is less frequent than ulnar or median involvement, but it can still occur, most often from compression of the nerve along the humeral spiral groove.

Clinically, patients may notice sensory changes over the dorsoradial hand and posterior forearm, and, depending on the lesion level, motor involvement can range from mild extensor weakness to a clear “wrist drop” with impaired finger extension.
The differential diagnosis includes posterior cord brachial plexopathy and C7 radiculopathy.
